fieldMarks: Long, slender weasel-family animal, about the size of a small cat: males 36-45 cm plus a 15-23 cm tail.
Grey head, light-brown back, very dark brown or black legs and tail.
Large eyes and cat-like ears; long, shiny fur. Females slightly smaller.
behavior: Usually solitary and mostly nocturnal, hunting most at dusk and dawn; active all winter and does not hibernate.
Moves easily in trees and scent-marks trails from tree to tree, but does most hunting on the ground; also swims well.
Eats mainly small mammals such as squirrels and other rodents, plus birds, fruit, nuts, insects and carrion.
Dens in hollow trees, crevices or vacant burrows.
habitat: Structurally complex, mature northern forest, including lodgepole pine, Douglas fir, spruce and mixed hardwood forest, at any elevation where such forest exists.
range: Northern North America from Newfoundland and Nova Scotia west to Alaska, and south in the Rocky Mountains and California; sporadic in New York, Michigan, Minnesota, Maine and Wisconsin, with reintroductions in Minnesota and Ontario.
